seo.title: Bangladeshi 6-Season Botanical Calendar (ষড়ঋতু) | Plantipedia
seo.description: Explore Bengal's six botanical seasons—Summer (গ্রীষ্ম), Monsoon (বর্ষা), Autumn (শরৎ), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত), Winter (শীত), and Spring (বসন্ত)—across Plantipedia Version 3.2's 50 curated 15-chapter monographs and 1,600,000+ (1.6M+) global flora index.
seo.keywords: Bangladeshi 6 seasons, Shororitu, Bengal flora calendar, Grishmo, Borsha, Shorot, Hemonto, Sheet, Boshonto, seasonal blooming plants, Plantipedia
seo.author: Plantipedia Botanical Archive
seo.ogDescription: Interactive phenological calendar tracking blooming, fruiting, and canopy transitions across the six Bengali seasons in Plantipedia Version 3.2.

banner.headline: Bangladeshi 6-Season Botanical Calendar
banner.subcopy: Bengal's alluvial ecosystems cycle through six distinct ecological seasons (Shororitu). Explore how flowering spikes, monsoon aquatic blooms, fruiting drupes, and cool-season ornamentals respond across the year.

seasons.imageAlt: Fiery scarlet Krishnochura blossoms flaring across sunlit summer skies during Grishmo
seasons.climateSummary: Intense solar radiation, warm westerly winds, and pre-monsoon Nor'wester storms (Kalboishakhi) catalyze rapid fruit sugar accumulation and intense essential-oil synthesis.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Peak Fruit Ripening (Madhumas) · Mango, Jackfruit, & Nocturnal Jasmine
ecologicalNotes: Known as 'Madhumas' (month of honey) as Mango and Jackfruit drupes and syncarps reach full sugar ripeness.
High evapotranspiration favors deep-rooted canopy trees, drought-hardy Neem drupes, and fragrant Beli blooms at dusk.

seasons.imageAlt: Golden-white Kadamba pincushion flowers blooming during rainy Borsha monsoon showers
seasons.climateSummary: Moisture-laden southwest monsoon winds inundate floodplains and haor basins, recharging soil aquifers and driving explosive vegetative growth.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Aquatic Macrophyte Spread · Bamboo Shoot Elongation · Rain-Lush Shrubs
ecologicalNotes: Floodwaters transform wetlands into emerald meadows where Shapla (Water Lily) and Lotus pads expand rapidly.
Bamboo rhizomes send up explosive shoots (Karul), while Ixora, Hibiscus, and Tea canopies flush vigorously.

seasons.imageAlt: Coral-tubed night-flowering Shiuli stars ushering in crisp Shorot autumn dawns
seasons.climateSummary: Crystal-clear skies dotted with white clouds alternate with warm humid sunshine as floodwaters gently recede across alluvial plains.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Mass Wetland Blooming · Sacred Lotus & National Water Lily Peak
ecologicalNotes: Clear, sunlit beels showcase peak blooming of Nymphaea nouchali (Shapla) and Nelumbo nucifera (Sacred Lotus).
Bamboo culms begin lignifying while Tulsi spikes attract late-season native bees.

seasons.imageAlt: Vivid papery Bougainvillea bracts stimulated by cooling late-autumn Hemonto winds
seasons.climateSummary: Morning mist, crisp night cooling, and drying post-monsoon soils trigger physiological stress cues that initiate winter flower buds.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Post-Rain Floral Induction · Bougainvillea Bracts & Marigold Beds
ecologicalNotes: Drying soils naturally induce floral bud initiation in Bougainvillea and arrest vegetative flushing in orchard trees.
Nurseries establish cool-season Marigold and Sunflower crops across fertile Gangetic loam.

seasons.imageAlt: Golden Marigold petals blooming richly during cool sunny Sheet winter mornings
seasons.climateSummary: Dry, cool northern breezes and mild sunlit afternoons create ideal conditions for long-lasting exhibition blooms and vernalization cues.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Cool-Season Ornamental Peak · Rose, Marigold, Orchid Spikes & Bougainvillea
ecologicalNotes: Cool nights trigger flower spikes on Phalaenopsis orchids and prolong crisp petal vibrancy in Roses and Marigolds.
Dry winter air slows Mango vegetative shoots, priming terminal buds for spring panicle emergence.

seasons.imageAlt: Golden Champaca spring blossoms awakening under warm Boshonto southern breezes
seasons.climateSummary: Gentle southern breezes ('Dokhina Batash') and warming golden days awaken dormant buds, copper foliage flushes, and pollinator guilds.
seasons.phenologyHighlight: Orchard Panicle Emergence · Mango Mukul, Neem Blossoms & First-Flush Tea
ecologicalNotes: Mango trees erupt in fragrant panicles (মুকুল) sustained by hoverflies and bees, while Neem briefly drops old leaves before bursting into white bloom.
Sylhet tea estates harvest prized First-Flush apical buds as Jackfruit trunks set young spikes.
